messages.author: 5c009c55dafaeed0
messages.subject: NA values using formatDistData
parts:
Hi,

I think I'm having a problem with "formatDistData" for use with gdistsamp. I'm inputting data in long form from a csv file, and some of my sites have NA values for a given Occasion. However, when I run the "formatDistData" command, all my NAs are replaced with 0s. And when I try to format this data into an "unmarkedFrameGDS", the summary tells me I have no NA values, but lots of 0s. I think this will change the density estimate, since it looks like I'm surveying more sites than I did and finding nothing at those sites, right? Am I using "formatDistData" wrong somehow? Below is the code that I'm using, and I've attached my sample dataset.

Thanks so much for any help anyone can give me,

Lucretia

temp1 <- read.csv("test.csv",header=T,sep=",", colClasses=c("factor","numeric","factor"))

gs.Dat <- formatDistData(temp1, distCol="dist",
transectNameCol="site", dist.breaks=seq(0,50,10),
occasionCol="Occ")

gs.Dat #gives a matrix with no NA values

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] NA values using formatDistData
parts:
Hi Lucretia,

I didn't anticipate that the function would be used this way. You will need to add NA's yourself, after formatting the data. 

Richard

Hi All,

I took a stab at altering the source code today to remedy the NA problem. 

This requires an additional input (an effort matrix of 1's for surveys and 0's for no surveys) but it does the job. 

I submitted a pull request on github (https://github.com/aurielfournier/unmarked/pull/1) but if it needs to be submitted an additional way let me know. 


Auriel
